In mathematics, a '''dendroidal set''' is a generalization of [[simplicial set]]s introduced by {{harvtxt|Moerdijk|Weiss|2007}}.
They have the same relation to (colored symmetric) [[operad]]s, also called [[symmetric multicategory|symmetric multicategories]],  that simplicial sets have to [[category theory|categories]].

==Definition==

A dendroidal set is a [[contravariant functor]] from Ω to [[set (category theory)|sets]], where Ω is the '''tree category''' consisting of finite rooted trees considered as operads, whose morphisms are operad morphisms. The trees are allowed to have some edges with a vertex on only one side; these are called outer edges, and the root is one of the outer edges.
